alert.raw: HIGH: Third-party OAuth app 'DataSyncPro' granted Mail.ReadWrite and Files.ReadWrite.All delegated permissions by c.patel. Subsequent bulk enumeration of 1,247 directory users and download of 14,200 email messages and 847 files via Microsoft Graph API. Data exfiltrated to external domain datasyncpro-backup.com.

telemetry.detail: c.patel granted 'DataSyncPro' (client_id: f82a3c9d-4411-4b2e-a6f1-8c3e7d2a9b0f) delegated permissions: Mail.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All, Contacts.Read, User.ReadBasic.All. Consent URI: login.microsoftonline.com (legitimate Azure AD endpoint).

telemetry.event: Access token issued by Azure AD
telemetry.detail: Bearer token issued, expiry: 1 hour. Granted scopes: Mail.ReadWrite Files.ReadWrite.All Contacts.Read User.ReadBasic.All. Refresh token also issued (90-day expiry).
Graph API GET /v1.0/users?$select=id,displayName,mail,jobTitle&$top=999 — returned 1,247 users (complete tenant directory). Second page fetched for remainder.
Graph API GET /v1.0/users/{id}/messages called for 15 different user IDs — NOT c.patel. Delegated token scope should restrict access to /me/ paths only. Possible over-privileged app registration.
14,200 messages downloaded via GET /v1.0/me/messages?$top=100 (paginated, 142 pages). Attachments included. Total size: 2.3 GB. Includes messages from Finance, Legal, and HR threads.
847 files recursively downloaded via /v1.0/me/drive/root/children. Directories accessed: /finance/, /legal/, /hr/, /exec-briefings/. Total: 4.1 GB.

HTTPS POST requests to api.datasyncpro-backup.com (IP: 91.195.240.117, AS: Frantech Solutions — known bulletproof hosting). Domain registered 3 days ago. Legitimate DataSyncPro.com resolves to 104.21.55.89 (Cloudflare). Different domains, different operators.

cachedVerdict.reasoning: This is a confirmed illicit OAuth consent grant attack. The attacker registered a malicious OAuth application named 'DataSyncPro' impersonating a legitimate backup tool, deceived c.patel into granting excessive permissions, then systematically exfiltrated email, files, and contacts via the Microsoft Graph API. The exfiltration destination is definitive: api.datasyncpro-backup.com is a typosquatted domain registered 3 days ago hosted on bulletproof infrastructure (Frantech Solutions), resolving to a completely different IP than the legitimate DataSyncPro.com service. Additionally, the app accessed mailboxes of 15 other users beyond c.patel — which delegated scope should not permit — indicating an over-privileged app registration likely designed specifically for tenant-wide data harvest. 6.4 GB of email and files including finance, legal, HR, and executive briefing directories have been exfiltrated. A 90-day refresh token remains active unless revoked.

timeline.event: Malicious OAuth app consent granted by c.patel
timeline.significance: Entry point: c.patel deceived into authorizing attacker's app via OAuth phishing link

timeline.event: Azure AD issues bearer token + 90-day refresh token
timeline.significance: Legitimate tokens issued to malicious app — attacker now inside the trust boundary with persistent access
Reconnaissance sweep — attacker mapping the org for targeting high-value accounts

timeline.event: Cross-user mailbox access beyond delegated scope
timeline.significance: App accessing other users' mail indicates over-privileged registration or tenant misconfiguration
Finance, legal, and HR email content — high-value intelligence and potential compliance breach
Highest-sensitivity directories targeted specifically — attacker knew exactly what to steal

timeline.event: 6.4 GB sent to typosquatted domain on bulletproof hosting
timeline.significance: Smoking gun: confirms malicious operator; data now in attacker's hands

evidence.signal: Exfil to datasyncpro-backup.com — typosquatted domain, 3 days old, bulletproof hosting
evidence.why_it_matters: Definitively distinguishes this from the legitimate DataSyncPro service; no legitimate app would route to Frantech Solutions infrastructure

evidence.signal: Cross-user mailbox access for 15 accounts beyond c.patel
evidence.why_it_matters: The attacker harvested credentials or tokens beyond the consenting user — potential tenant-wide compromise vector
Systematic reconnaissance indicates a sophisticated attacker building a target map, not a misconfigured sync tool

evidence.signal: Finance, legal, HR, exec-briefings directories specifically targeted
evidence.why_it_matters: Attacker exhibited prior knowledge of directory structure — suggests reconnaissance or insider-assisted targeting

containment.action: Revoke all tokens for the DataSyncPro app registration immediately
containment.target: Azure AD Enterprise Applications — client_id: f82a3c9d-4411-4b2e-a6f1-8c3e7d2a9b0f
containment.rationale: Terminates bearer token AND the 90-day refresh token; token revocation is near-instant in Azure AD

containment.action: Block at email gateway, web proxy, and DNS
containment.rationale: Prevent any in-flight exfiltration from completing and block future callback attempts from the 90-day refresh token

containment.action: Audit all tenant users for DataSyncPro consent grants
containment.target: All M365 users — check Azure AD Enterprise Applications and OAuth consent logs
containment.rationale: Illicit consent attacks frequently target multiple users; revoke consent for all affected accounts

containment.action: Notify Legal, DPO, and Privacy team
containment.rationale: 6.4 GB including finance/legal/HR/executive data likely triggers GDPR Article 33 (72-hour notification) and CCPA breach disclosure obligations

containment.action: Export and preserve Azure AD unified audit logs
containment.target: Microsoft 365 Security & Compliance Center — audit log export
containment.rationale: Default log retention is 90 days; export immediately to preserve forensic record of all Graph API calls made by the malicious app

next_steps.step: Leverage active 90-day refresh token to re-establish access after initial revocation attempt
Expand OAuth phishing campaign targeting additional high-value accounts in the tenant
Use harvested 1,247-user directory to launch targeted spearphishing at finance and legal teams

cachedVerdict.ciso_summary: A criminal actor created a fake application disguised as a legitimate business tool and tricked one of our employees into granting it full access to company email and files, resulting in the theft of over 6 gigabytes of confidential data including financial reports, legal documents, and executive briefings. We have immediately cut off the application's access to our systems and blocked the server where the stolen data was being sent. Because the stolen data included sensitive business and personal information, our legal and data privacy teams are now assessing whether we are required to notify employees, customers, and regulators within the applicable statutory timeframes.
cachedVerdict.summary: Illicit OAuth consent grant: malicious 'DataSyncPro' app exfiltrated 14,200 emails (2.3 GB) and 847 files (4.1 GB — finance/legal/HR) via Microsoft Graph API to a typosquatted bulletproof domain. Revoke app tokens now. Legal/privacy breach notification likely required.
